claims.claim: Under B_off=0, R=0, identical edge-examination accounting, direct predecessor access shifts the sampled online feasible-set frontier relative to successor-only forward BFS.
claims.scope: finite arithmetic graph; M in {30,300,3000}; three seeds
limits: one graph family in the native-access comparison

claims.claim: Exhaustive online predecessor emulation using only successor operations does not recover the native predecessor frontier at the tight budgets tested.
limits: not an optimality proof over all successor-only encodings
claims.next_discriminating_test: Test stronger state representations and independent graph families.

claims.claim: A fixed successor-only executor can shift its online frontier by using target-oblivious multi-step macro state without changing transition topology.
claims.scope: affine, permutation, and opaque finite graph controls; macro2/3/4; seeds 17,23,41

claims.claim: A target-oblivious reverse adjacency index reproduces the native bidirectional online success pattern and minimum online budgets exactly in the tested finite arithmetic graph, at the cost of B_off=3M and R=3M.
limits: the reverse-index consumer uses generic stored-neighbor traversal
whether that traversal is part of the fixed substrate must be specified explicitly
claims.interpretation: direct predecessor access can be represented as frozen state if the substrate admits generic stored-relation traversal

claims.claim: A target-oblivious all-pairs next-action table used by a fixed successor executor can reduce the maximum sampled post-instance budget to 9, 13, and 17 for M=30,100,300 respectively, at approximately O(M^2) offline construction and storage.
limits: does not address scalable compact representations
claims.interpretation: online computation can be traded for offline computation and persistent representation without changing successor execution semantics

claims.claim: Mechanism change should be judged by whether it adds a Pareto-frontier point under a fully specified resource and substrate contract; a mechanism-name difference alone does not establish capability expansion.
limits: generic state-relation traversal boundary is not yet fully formalized
claims.next_discriminating_test: Specify the minimal generic state-indexed relation-lookup primitive, then determine whether it is already contained in the fixed substrate or is itself a new transition primitive.
